_comment: Register pointers whose cited LINE CONTENT differs from the revision that wrote them, each with a written `reason` saying which PR re-pins it or why nothing does. The screen FAILS on any drift not listed here and reports entries that no longer drift as STALE (non-failing, prune them). `regLines` are the register sentences the cite silences — the screen matches on cite, so one entry can cover several. Regenerate preserving reasons: node scripts/check-register-drift.mjs --update

entries.reason: Read-log, not a pointer: PP-055 lists the auto-backup line set (55, 147, 243, 256-257, 297) as ranges somebody read, and #2441 declined to re-pin it for exactly that reason — re-pinning would invent an intent the entry never stated. Listed here so the decision is on the record instead of silent drift.

History, not a live pointer: the register sentence listed in regLines (currently :117, re-derived by --update — the prose used to call it :85) is PP-068's bullet reporting the coordinate as it found it — `docs/README.md:71` was where the README paragraph sat then, and it now sits at `docs/README.md:75`, which PP-072 (#2556) re-pinned to the rule's :4651. Re-writing PP-068's sentence would falsify the measurement it reports. #2534 (PP-070) and #2507 (PP-065) re-pin the same live cite from their own trees, so whichever docs PR merges last re-derives this entry; prune it the day the README names the rule by heading text instead of a line number.

Chronic, not accidental: the register sentences in regLines (:33 PP-073's header bullet, :49 PP-072's) both quote the README's own re-pin of the pointer INTO the register — so any entry that adds register header text moves the line the pointer names, and this cite reads as drift by construction. PP-072 (#2556, merged) minted it with the rule at :4651; PP-073 (#2567) re-pinned the same sentence to :4774 because PP-072's own section is what moved it, and **#2566** re-pins it again to :4840 because its own residual bullet sits above the rule — the eleventh such re-pin. #2534 (PP-070) and #2507 (PP-065) are open re-pinning it from their own trees, so whichever docs PR merges last re-derives this entry. Prune it the day the README points at the rule by heading text instead of a line number.
